items.question: For each of the APIs listed below — can you walk us through what DAS actually uses them for? Not the implementation specifics, but the business purpose each one serves and which features or endpoints are actively in use. We want to understand what is used for what, so we can run a more focused research pass and identify where there might be room for improvements or a better fit.
items.context:
Resolved 2026-06-18 — DAS engineering walkthrough complete. Business purpose and actively-used endpoints documented per API in individual wiki pages; CDP field coverage targets (launch vs. later) established. Original context: Refined at the 2026-06-12 sync — the core of the ask: what does DAS extract from each API TODAY vs what the API offers for potential future integration (e.g., is everything in Twilio fair game later, or do we design around current capture)? Dan Aston took the list to engineering. We've mapped these from the Integration Explorer and have a working sense of which products they're tied to, but we don't have visibility into the actual features or endpoints being exercised. The list below is grouped by category with our current assumption of which DAS product uses each API — correct us where we're off.

Ad Platforms — Meta / Facebook Marketing API (Media Logix, Social Logix, LotVantage) · Google Ads API (Media Logix) · Microsoft / Bing Ads API (Media Logix) · Amazon Ads API (Media Logix) · TikTok Ads API (Media Logix) · YouTube Data / Analytics API (Media Logix, LotVantage) · Reddit Ads (Media Logix)

Communications — Twilio (CDXP, ETS, Mobile Review Surge) · SendGrid (shared-svcs, Response Logix, ETS) · MailGun (CDXP) · Mandrill / Mailchimp Transactional (Response Path, Response Logix) · ETS Dashboard API (ETS) · Rocket.Chat (ETS, AI Engage Messaging, Response Path) · LiveJoin3 Service (ETS LiveJoin) · ETS Facebook Messenger + SMS Proxy (ETS) · Microsoft Graph / Outlook (Radar)

DMS / CRM — Salesforce (Account Mgmt API, Social Logix, TheWire) · Microsoft Dynamics 365 (Social Logix) · Tekion DMS (Social Logix Review Surge, CDXP)

Data Enrichment — MaxMind GeoIP2 (CDXP) · Experian Conquest (CDXP) · NeverBounce (CDXP)

Marketplace — eBay API (LotVantage) · Facebook Marketplace (LotVantage) · Craigslist (LotVantage)

Reviews — CallRevu (CDXP) · CarGurus (Social Logix) · Cars.com (Social Logix) · Carfax (Social Logix, LotVantage) · DealerRater + Edmunds (Social Logix) · Vendasta + Mozenda (Social Logix) · Recall Masters (CDXP)

Social / Listings — Soci (Social Logix) · Yext (Social Logix Local)

Billing — CyberSource (LotVantage) · Zuora (LotVantage, DWRPT reporting) · QuickBooks (LotVantage)

items.question: Can Conflict get read access to the DWRPT database?
items.context: Granted 2026-06-12. Used for the Common Client ID audit and as the reporting-parity reference only — per the access close-out decision, DWRPT is not a CDP ingestion source. The CDP targets the original feeds upstream of EDW/DWRPT.

items.question: Which SSIS jobs produce raw vs. post-processed data — and which source tables should CDP pull from?
items.context: Superseded 2026-06-12 by the ingestion direction: the CDP pulls from original sources (event intake + Airflow batch on the feeds that enter DAS), not from any SSIS landing tables. 5 of 13 jobs were mapped from etl/ code along the way; per-field sourcing lives in the field-source matrix.

items.question: What is the schema and quality of the Common Client ID implementation?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-18 — we are building our own Common Client ID from first principles (deterministic-first identity engine, Option A locked 2026-06-17). DAS's CCID is at most a migration/backfill signal, not the foundation (objective 7); we have enough from the DWRPT access already granted to weigh it. The schema/access/ID-assignment ask to Dan + Ron is dropped — no DAS deliverable needed. Original framing (2026-06-12): identity resolution is a first-principles Conflict design; DAS has zero cross-system resolution today and CCID is recent, low-investment, and unproven (cleanliness issues already found).
items.owner: Conflict (audit) / Dan Aston (access) / Ron Mulder (ID-assignment logic)

items.question: Which source systems have Common Client ID coverage, and which are still unjoined?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-18 — we have enough. The per-source identity-signal inventory (email, phone, address, VIN, CCID where present) is captured from discovery; sources without any deterministic key get probabilistic matching regardless of CCID, so exhaustive CCID-coverage mapping is not a design gate. Orphan identifiers with nothing to join to today (e.g., Facebook IDs from reviews) are first-class — stored, attributed, resolvable later (objective 9).

items.question: Why has Mileone_reward_member failed 100% of the time over 20 runs? Is it safe to exclude from CDP scope?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-12 — out of CDP scope. This is DAS-internal tech debt in a pipeline slated for retirement; the CDP ingests from original sources, so a dead legacy job is DAS's operational concern, not a design input. Flagged to Rick in the job-descriptions ask for DAS's own housekeeping.

items.question: What is the dependency graph between the 13 SSIS jobs? Which jobs must complete before others can start?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-12 — not needed. The DAG matters for operating or modernizing the pipeline in place; the direction (per DAS) is replacement, with the CDP ingesting from original sources. DAS operates the legacy ordering until retirement. Partial DAG already inferred from etl/ code if ever useful.

items.question: What is the accurate description of each SSIS job — what source data does it process and what does it produce?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-12 — substantially answered by the full etl/ inventory (docs/etl-data-inventory.md, 231 objects / 20 modules), which supersedes the old 5-of-13 framing: CustomerValue, DDE, LeadSource_LeadPerformance, and JuiceReporting_CDXPCustomers map to documented reporting-layer modules (all feeding Juicebox, which the CDP will not replicate); MileOne Unsubscribe and SmartSuppression map plausibly to Email/Sync suppression procs. Residual unknowns (Conquest_Mailing, dead Mileone_reward_member) are peripheral legacy ops. Rick's relayed ask stays as a courtesy backstop. One requirement carried forward: suppression/consent data is a CDP data-model category in its own right.

items.question: What replaces Juicebox? Power BI, Metabase, custom CDP reporting?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-12 — this is Conflict's to answer, not an open question for DAS. Tracked as the Phase 1 reporting-platform decision in the project plan; deferred per the discovery deck so it does not block Phase 1. The 14 CDXP-Live client commitments remain the acceptance context.

items.question: Which Juicebox reports should we sample as reference patterns for CDP reporting?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-12 — CDP reporting will be designed from first principles, not by replicating Juicebox reports. No sampling exercise. The 14 CDXP-Live client commitments remain relevant only as acceptance criteria, not as design templates.

items.question: What is the full architecture of ai.das-technology.com — who maintains it, what model, how is it deployed?
items.context: Closed 2026-06-12 — not needed for CDP design. The relationship inverts: today's agents query DWRPT; once the CDP is the source of truth, AI features draw from the CDP. Current-stack details become relevant at Phase 3 (AI/ML integration), not before.

items.question: (Optional) Would DAS like us to sample the 14 client-facing CDXP-Live reports to model CDP reporting parity?
items.context: Not required. CDP reporting is a first-principles Conflict design, not a Juicebox replication; a sample only sharpens parity modeling in the Scoping deliverable if DAS wants it. Was a timeline-only discovery step with no owner; reframed as an optional DAS question 2026-06-13. CLOSED 2026-06-18 — Leo’s decision: NO. "We saw enough in the live demo and meeting, we have screenshots." No separate report-sampling exercise needed.
